topics.title: U.S. and China cut tariffs
topics.summary: The United States and China agreed to trim tariffs on about $60 billion in goods, including agriculture and household items, while extending their trade truce.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two rivals suddenly lower tariffs, who starts planning cheaper snacks and who wonders what they traded behind closed doors?

topics.title: Iran talks continue through mediators
topics.summary: U.S. and Iranian representatives were expected to hold separate mediator-led talks in New York after Washington dismissed Tehran's latest proposal over sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz.
topics.discussionPrompt: When talks happen in separate rooms, who thinks that keeps things calm and who says everyone should just sit at one table?

topics.title: UK airbase arrests investigated
topics.summary: British police said five suspects arrested near RAF Fairford were British nationals as investigators examined an explosives case and possible international links.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a quiet airbase suddenly becomes headline news, who wants every detail and who immediately starts guessing how security missed it?

topics.title: Starship heads toward orbit
topics.summary: SpaceX launched Starship on its 14th test flight, with the vehicle reported as the first in the program aimed at reaching orbit.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a giant rocket finally aims for orbit, who is counting engineering milestones and who just wants the launch replay on loop?

topics.title: Bangkok shelters fill after floods
topics.summary: Thousands of Bangkok residents stayed in shelters as officials assessed flood damage estimated above $320 million after heavy rains disrupted parts of the city.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a city floods, who focuses on helping neighbors first and who wants to redesign the entire drainage map?

topics.title: South Korea questions Ukraine disclosure
topics.summary: South Korea summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador after Kyiv disclosed the transfer of captured North Korean soldiers to Seoul, saying the matter was meant to stay confidential.
topics.discussionPrompt: When allies disagree over what should stay private, who says transparency matters and who reaches for the diplomatic apology template?

topics.title: Pope Leo wraps France visit
topics.summary: Pope Leo was expected to address Europe's role in the world in Metz, with remarks touching on peace in Ukraine and concerns over rising nationalism.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a pope gives Europe homework, who nods seriously and who asks whether anyone actually turns in the assignment?

topics.title: Ukraine allies hear NATO warning
topics.summary: NATO's top commander in Europe told EU lawmakers that Russia's activity is aimed at weakening allies' will to keep supporting Ukraine.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a commander says morale is the target, who talks strategy and who checks whether everyone is getting enough sleep?

topics.title: UK homebuilders rise on buyer plan
topics.summary: Shares in British homebuilders climbed after a new support scheme for first-time buyers was announced, lifting hopes for demand in the housing market.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a housing plan boosts builders, who sees opportunity and who immediately asks whether first-time buyers actually feel helped?

topics.title: Sami history exhibition opens
topics.summary: An exhibition in Kiruna, Sweden highlights Sami lives and history as a long-awaited report on state abuses against Indigenous people is handed over.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a museum exhibit arrives with a difficult public report, who wants quiet reflection and who wants the government response first?
